decision: Direct AFOL invocation is the local-operator authority path. Explicit agent and remote contexts are restrictive policy modes only. Flags, environment values, task owners, and session actors are not authenticated identity or authority credentials.
rationale: The CLI cannot isolate a process with ordinary write access under the same Unix account through in-process checks alone.
The current red tests prove explicit restricted-mode behavior only. They do not prove caller identity or omitted-marker safety.
A launcher-issued artifact would require an external trust root, protected issuer state, revocation, replay state, and prevention of direct AFOL execution. None exists in this repository.
Adding a token, daemon, key system, or wrapper without that external boundary would rename self-attestation instead of creating authority.

required_fields.issuer_trust_boundary: The deployment local-operator entry path is the authority source. AFOL does not authenticate it in-process. Same-account processes with project write access are outside the CLI isolation boundary.
required_fields.audience: Direct AFOL invocation for the local operator. Managed agent and remote entries are restrictive-mode invocations only.
required_fields.expiry_renewal: Policy mode is per-process and ends with the process. No durable grant or renewal protocol exists.
required_fields.revocation: Deployment removes the constrained tool entry, generic shell access, or project write access. AFOL has no same-account in-process revocation mechanism.
required_fields.replay_protection: Not applicable because C01 introduces no bearer artifact. Locks, task IDs, owners, and actors are not replay protection.
required_fields.verification: AFOL resolves one canonical action policy before dispatch and applies it to an immutable execution-mode context. Explicit restricted inputs may reduce access only.
required_fields.audit: C01 creates no persistent policy-decision audit. A denial returns the existing structured approval-required envelope with the normalized action and exit code 2 before handler I/O. Allowed actions retain existing command-specific evidence behavior.
required_fields.local_operator_fallback: Direct invocation is the local-operator path, not an agent fallback. Restricted mode cannot upgrade itself through flags, environment, owner, or actor labels.
required_fields.test_shell_policy: done --test-shell remains local-operator-only and absent from agent or remote tool catalogs, including generic shell entries. Command persistence needs separate redaction scope.

classifications.direct_invocation: local-operator deployment boundary, not authenticated human identity
classifications.omitted_markers: select the direct local-operator path; they do not prove that an agent is absent

forbidden: daemon, service, key store, launcher binary, host-account or container configuration
src/project-template/**, generated payloads, manifests, provider credentials, and legacy runtime surfaces
cli/commands/adapter.ts; adapter denial is enforced by the central pre-dispatch policy
implementation_boundary.denial_record: non-persistent structured approval-required envelope with exit code 2

acceptance_limits: R-02 and SEC-001, SEC-003, and SEC-004 explicit restricted-mode tests may become green.
SEC-002 must not be claimed as an identity guarantee.
Same-account isolation, authentication, cross-host ownership, revocation, and replay protection remain unclaimed.
